question: Neurogenic shock following a thoracic spinal cord injury classically presents with hypotension AND bradycardia, unlike haemorrhagic shock which produces tachycardia.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Neurogenic shock is caused by loss of descending sympathetic pathways in the spinal cord, producing hypotension from vasodilation AND bradycardia from unopposed vagal tone. Haemorrhagic shock produces compensatory tachycardia. The bradycardia in neurogenic shock is a critical diagnostic clue.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Neurogenic shock = loss of sympathetic tone → vasodilation (hypotension) + unopposed vagal tone (bradycardia). This paradoxical combination distinguishes it from haemorrhagic shock. Warm, dry skin (vasodilated) vs cool, clammy (haemorrhagic) is an additional distinguishing feature.
